questions.question: List five elements a route map must have and explain why landmarks are placed at turning points.
questions.expected_answer: Title; start and end points; the route line with arrows; north arrow; key; (approximate distances or scale). Landmarks at turning points tell the traveller exactly where to change direction, because they are easy to recognise and do not move.

questions.question: Rewrite this vague direction as a clear one: Go down there and turn by the shop, it's a bit further.
questions.expected_answer: Example: Leave the school gate and walk north along School Road for about 300 metres to the Shell garage. Turn right, east, into Main Road and walk about 500 metres. The clinic is on your right, a white building opposite the post office. (Answer should include direction, landmark and distance.)

questions.question: Describe two ways to estimate distance without measuring, and explain why estimates should be rounded and include units.
questions.expected_answer: Pacing: count steps (about 1 500 steps per kilometre). Time: walking about 4-5 km per hour, so about 12-15 minutes per kilometre. Familiar lengths such as a 100 m soccer field. Estimates are not precise, so exact figures are misleading; units are needed because a number alone could mean metres, steps or minutes.
